item.title: Today in Sweden: A roundup of the latest news on Tuesday
item.description: Swedish government sends welfare reform to law council, wolf cull blocked by courts, and other news from Sweden on Tuesday.

item.title: Will Sweden have a white Christmas this year?
item.description: With just a little over a week left until Christmas, the weather forecasts for the holiday season are coming in.

item.title: Leader of Swedish Moderate youth wing criticises work permit reforms
item.description: The leader of the Moderate Party's youth wing has called on the government to allow rejected asylum seekers who have successfully switched to a work permit to stay in Sweden, in a sign of a split in the ruling party over labour migration.

item.title: Swedish greenhouse gas emissions rise 7 percent
item.description: Greenhouse gas emissions in Sweden rose by seven percent in 2024, the largest rise since 1990, in large part due to increased use of diesel, the Swedish Environmental Protection Agency said on Tuesday.

item.title: Stockholm on track for darkest December since 1934
item.description: The Swedish capital has recorded just a half-hour of sunlight in the first half of this month, putting it on track for the darkest December since 1934 if the trend continues.

item.title: Swedish word of the day: mula
item.description: Today's word of the day is mula – a word you are unlikely to hear unless you regularly hang out with young Swedes.

item.title: How and when do you buy a Christmas tree in Sweden?
item.description: Three million households in Sweden buy a Christmas tree every year, either from one of the stalls that pop up in town squares across the country, from an out-of-town retailer, or direct from a grower. Here's how to get your tree.

item.title: When do you start saying Merry Christmas in Sweden?
item.description: There are a surprising number of unwritten rules when it comes to greeting people throughout the Christmas season. So when should you say god jul, and when is it better to wish someone a 'good continuation' or a 'good end' instead?

item.title: Workers dismissed from Sweden's Northvolt to get EU aid
item.description: The EU has voted to compensate the more than 5,000 people who lost their jobs when the Swedish electric battery producer Northvolt went bankrupt in March.

item.title: Courts in Sweden slam proposal to revoke permanent residency permits
item.description: Four of Sweden's highest legal authorities have advised the government to drop a proposal to revoke permanent residency permits, warning that it risks massive costs, would overwhelm the legal system, and threatens important legal principles.
